headline: Prosecute the postal offenders
summary: Roosevelt tells Knox the Post Office wrongdoers must be prosecuted and takes responsibility for Payne's actions amid heavy press criticism. He writes Lyman Abbott about peonage of Black workers in Georgia and Russia's stance in Manchuria, where Russia refuses to open the ports.

headline: No presidential name for a Jerusalem model
summary: Roosevelt lunches with Speyer and Knox and has John McCall to dinner and overnight, with Cortelyou joining them. He writes John Proctor about irregularities at the Washington post office and wires Joseph Burton that he refuses to endorse a for-profit model of Jerusalem planned for the 1904 fair.

events.detail: McCall dines and stays the night; Cortelyou at dinner
Letter to Proctor and telegram to Burton

headline: Leupp sent to Indian Territory
summary: Roosevelt lunches with Melville Stone and Ware and dines with Benjamin Ide Wheeler, the Hays, the Jusserands and Wayne MacVeagh; Wheeler stays the night. He asks Francis Leupp to serve as an impartial investigator of the Oklahoma Indian reservations.

letters.topic: Asks him to look impartially into Indian reservations in Oklahoma

headline: Supper at Great Falls
summary: Roosevelt lunches with Crane, Cooley, Proctor and Major Carson, then dines at Great Falls, Virginia, with Pinchot, Garfield and Proctor. Letters touch the postal probe, Ray Stannard Baker's articles, the press, and a false coal-strike story. Hanna will not give up the national chairmanship.

headline: Lunch for Sir Thomas Lipton
summary: Roosevelt hosts a lunch for yachtsman Sir Thomas Lipton with Moody, Andrew D. White, General Corbin, Hanna and others, and hears Perkins on Wall Street's view of his finance bills. He gives Perkins the pen that signed the Commerce and Labor act and spends the evening at Hay's with Douglas Robinson.

headline: Summer begins at Oyster Bay

headline: Sunday at Sagamore Hill
summary: Roosevelt is home at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: No delay on Alaska
summary: Lyman Abbott comes to lunch and Joe Bishop stays the night. Roosevelt tells Hay the Alaska boundary must be settled without delay, and writes Platt on New York appointments.

letters.topic: Unspecified
Settle the Alaska boundary promptly
Patronage in New York State

Kermit departs for a Black Hills hunt with Bullock

headline: Angry at Russia over the Kishinev petition
summary: Sagamore Hill fills with guests, among them niece Eleanor, Gifford Pinchot and Beekman Winthrop, and Beveridge comes to dinner. Roosevelt writes Francis Loomis about a petition to Russia protesting the Kishinev massacre, and tells Hay he is angered by Russia's impertinence.

headline: Quiet day at home
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: Opening the Pacific cable
summary: On the Fourth of July Roosevelt speaks at Huntington, Long Island, to celebrate the newly completed cable across the Pacific, and sends a message across it to Governor Taft in Manila. He defends his irrigation policy to Ray Stannard Baker and tells George Holls he will act in the national interest whatever foreign powers think.

Cables a message to Taft in Manila

headline: Sunday at Sagamore Hill
summary: Roosevelt is at home; nothing else is recorded.

headline: Hay at Sagamore Hill
summary: Secretary Hay, Winthrop Chanler and Grant La Farge are guests. Over lunch with Hanna, Fairbanks and others, Roosevelt and Hay take up Alaska, Manchuria and the petition to the Czar on behalf of Russia's Jews. He tells Seth Bullock that Ted and his cousin George will reach Deadwood on August 20 to hunt.

letters.topic: Urges a rest rather than resignation

summary: From the Hudson, Roosevelt calls on John Burroughs at his cabin, Slabsides, in West Park, New York, then returns to Oyster Bay.
